topic: Balancing Redox Reactions: Half Reaction Method
title: Half Reaction Method Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
Pay a friend fifty rupees and two messages pop up: fifty debited, fifty credited. Two halves of one deal. In this animated lesson for Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 7, Redox Reactions) Aarav cuts a long equation in two and balances one half at a time.

You will see every redox reaction split into an oxidation half (gives electrons) and a reduction half (takes electrons). On the molecule bench iron(II) gives one electron, then we balance the dichromate half in four steps with a live counter: main atom, oxygen with water, hydrogen with H+, charge with 6 electrons. We match the electrons on a scale (iron half times six), add the halves and watch the electrons cancel. Then: the half reaction (ion electron) method in order, acid vs basic solutions, permanganate and iodide in a basic solution, the electrons-last trap, an original JEE Main pattern question, a recap card and three questions to check yourself. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.

This is Episode 75 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students.

In this video:
